correctness.rationale: I reconstructed the wreath-product automorphism group from intrinsic Hamming graph edge directions, and hence the invariant per-coordinate marker-equality/status counts defining each stabilizer orbit. Every status vector is realizable for q>=4, so the stars-and-bars and multinomial formulas include all boundary types n_pi=0. For each mark a_j, counting refinement identifies distances truncated at t+1 after t rounds, hence full three-distance vectors after d-1 rounds. A single extra round recovers the multiplicities of neighbour distance-vector displacements e_S-e_T. On three marker labels, displacements for distinct nonempty partition blocks identify all two- and three-block coordinate statuses, while the distance vector and total n_pi recover the one-block status. Thus round d determines every orbit profile; equivariance gives the reverse inclusion. A separately implemented Hamming adjacency/refinement versus exact orbit-status checker passed 77 new finite triples for q=4,5,6 and dimensions 2–4; that bounded test is not the proof of universal quantifiers.
